claims.explanation: Piperacetazine is a phenothiazine antipsychotic that, beyond dopamine receptor antagonism, directly binds and inhibits the PAX3::FOXO1 fusion protein and inhibits squalene epoxidase (SQLE), and its transcriptional signature resembles EGFR inhibitors. Selectivity is therefore most plausibly driven by dependence on PAX3::FOXO1 fusion (alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma), by SQLE/cholesterol-pathway dependence, and by EGFR/MAPK pathway addiction, with dopamine-receptor and phenothiazine-off-target effects contributing more broadly.

transcriptional signature most similar to EGFR inhibitor tyrphostin-AG-494; EGFR-addicted lines may respond
annotated dopamine receptor antagonist; DRD2-expressing lines may be more sensitive
phenothiazine dopamine receptor antagonism may contribute to growth inhibition
phenothiazines antagonize serotonin receptors; expression may modulate response
phenothiazine alpha-adrenergic antagonism may contribute to off-target effects
similarity to acetylcholine receptor antagonist AQ-RA741 suggests cholinergic dependence
similarity to sodium channel blocker disopyramide suggests ion-channel dependence
similarity to ACE inhibitor moexipril suggests RAS-pathway dependence
CASP7 downregulation in virtual cell response; low caspase-7 may reduce apoptotic sensitivity
